title: Menumancer scene
description: A Menumancer scene: layers drawn bottom to top over a seamless loop.

$schema.description: The JSON Schema of this file, for editors. The engine ignores it.

format.description: Always "menumancer.scene": marks the file as a scene.

version.description: Format version. Older versions are upgraded on load; a newer one needs a newer Menumancer.

loop.description: Loop length and frame rate: the last frame flows into the first.

seed.description: Seed of the scene's randomness: the same scene and seed always give the same frames.

camera.description: Camera: zoom, drift (parallax by layer depth), field of view for 3D models.

render.description: Frame quality: antialiasing, HDR, tonemapping, bloom, atmosphere, motion blur, depth of field.

lighting.description: Scene lights for layers that are lit.

live.description: What the scene reacts to as a live wallpaper (sound, mouse). No effect on the Dota video.

layers.description: Layers bottom to top: the first is drawn first.

effects.description: Effects on the finished frame over all layers (fog, colour grading, vignette), in order.

exposed.description: Params the user of the scene gets as sliders.

settings.description: Settings the user of the scene picks (colours, numbers, switches, choices, text) and the values each drives.

assets.description: Files of the scene with the source and licence of each.

id.description: Layer name, unique in the whole scene (groups included): Latin letters, digits, - and _.

depth.description: Depth: 0 for the far background, more for nearer layers. Camera drift moves deeper layers more.

blend.description: How the layer blends with what is below it.

desktopOnly.description: Drawn only by the live wallpaper; the Dota video and previews without live data skip it.

transform.description: Offset, scale and rotation of the layer.

attach.description: Pins the layer to an attachment point of a puppet layer: it moves with that point's bone.

effects.description: Effects of the layer, in order.

params.description: Params read by the layer's shader, particle preset or node.

ParticleAttractor.description: Particles are pulled towards a control point, or pushed away with a negative strength.

point.description: The id of a control point of the system.

strength.description: The pull, units per second per second; negative pushes away.

radius.description: Radius beyond which the point does not pull, units; 0: everywhere.

ParticleChild.description: A particles layer whose particles are born from this system's particles: along the path, at birth or at death.

on.description: When the child emits: follow (along the path), spawn (at birth) or death (at death).

layer.description: The id of the child particles layer.

count.description: Child particles per birth or death, or per second for follow.

ParticleControlPoint.description: A named point operators refer to; it may follow the cursor on the desktop.

cursor.description: The point follows the cursor on the desktop; the Dota video holds it at "at".

ParticleDepth.description: Particles in depth: their distance behind the layer and, with perspective, projection by the scene camera.

z.description: Distance behind the layer's plane at birth, units; 0 is on the plane, negative is nearer.

perspective.description: Project particles with the scene camera's field of view (camera.fov): farther ones look smaller.

ParticleOperator.description: A force or limit on every particle while it lives; "type" picks it.

ParticleSpeedCap.description: No particle moves faster than max.

max.description: The highest speed, units per second.

operators.description: Forces and limits on every particle while it lives, in order: turbulence, vortex, attract, speedCap.

controlPoints.description: Named points operators refer to; a point may follow the cursor on the desktop.

children.description: Particles layers whose particles are born from this system's particles.

ParticleTurbulence.description: A noise field that pushes particles around in swirls.

strength.description: The push, units per second per second.

scale.description: Size of the field's swirls, units.

cycles.description: How many times the field changes over the loop: a whole number, so the loop closes.

ParticleVortex.description: Particles circle a point, faster or slower with the distance.

outer.description: Radius beyond which the vortex does not act, units; 0: everywhere.

speedInner.description: Speed round the middle at the inner radius, units per second; positive is clockwise.

rate.description: Speed: 1 as in the puppet file, 0.5 half as fast. A number or keys; the clip advances by the rate summed over time.

blend.description: Weight 0..1: a normal layer's share in the mix, an additive layer's strength. A number or keys.

visible.description: Whether the layer plays: true or false, or keys of 1 (on) and 0 (off) with "ease": "hold".

blendIn.description: Seconds over which the layer fades in when it turns on; 0 uses blendTime.

blendOut.description: Seconds over which the layer fades out when it turns off; 0 uses blendTime.

blendTime.description: Fade in and out, seconds, where blendIn or blendOut is 0; 0 switches at once.

path.description: Path relative to the scene folder with /, such as "assets/bg.png".

SceneSetting.description: A setting the user of the scene picks (colour, number, switch, choice, text) and the values it drives.

id.description: Setting name: Latin letters, digits, - and _.

kind.description: What the setting holds: color, number, switch, choice or text.

value.description: The value as picked (the default for a new user): a colour, a number, true/false, an option's value or text.

options.description: What a choice offers, in order.

drives.description: The values the setting sets: value paths, each optionally only when the setting equals an option.

path.description: Value path the setting drives, such as "flag.color", "rain.visible" or "fog.params.density".

when.description: The setting's value at which this on/off target is on (an option, or "true"/"false"); absent: the target takes the setting's value.

ShaderEffect.description: A scene's own HLSL shader: the source file, its pictures and what to draw when it cannot run.

file.description: The HLSL source file in the scene folder (.hlsl), listed in assets.

textures.description: Pictures the shader reads as texture0..texture7: a scene file, "$layer" (the layer's picture) or "$under" (the frame under the layer); null reads white.

fallback.description: What to draw when the shader cannot run: skip (without it) or hide (hide the layer).

VideoTexture.description: A video file playing inside an image layer; the layer's picture is shown where it cannot play.

file.description: The video file in the scene folder (.webm, .mp4), listed in assets.

fps.description: Frames per second to play at; absent: the file's own rate.

offset.description: Seconds into the video at the start of the loop.

color.description: "#rrggbb", "#rrggbbaa" or [r, g, b] / [r, g, b, a] in 0..1.

colorValue.description: A colour: constant, a wave { "wave" }, keyframes { "keys" }, a formula { "expr" } or a script { "script" } / { "scriptFile" }.

scriptFile.description: The script file in the scene folder (.js), listed in assets.

inputs.description: What the script reads besides the time: mouse, audio, clock, media, settings.<id> or another value's path.

numberValue.description: A number: constant, a wave { "wave" }, keyframes { "keys" }, a formula { "expr" } or a script { "script" } / { "scriptFile" }.

scriptFile.description: The script file in the scene folder (.js), listed in assets.

inputs.description: What the script reads besides the time: mouse, audio, clock, media, settings.<id> or another value's path.

param.description: A param read by the layer's shader, preset or node: a number, a vector, a colour (each may be animated), a string or a switch.

switchValue.description: On or off: true or false, or a number value of 1 (on) and 0 (off), such as keys with "ease": "hold".

vectorValue.description: A vector: constant, a wave { "wave" }, keyframes { "keys" }, a formula { "expr" } or a script { "script" } / { "scriptFile" }.

scriptFile.description: The script file in the scene folder (.js), listed in assets.
